coarse_subsets.notes: Managers + professionals + clerical support. Conservative *heuristic subset*, not proven exact SOC coverage or calibrated cognitive share.
Adds all technicians and associate professionals: over-inclusive for some mappings, under-inclusive for sales occupations.
Adds all service AND sales jobs even though U.S. SOC 41 includes sales but not all personal/protective services; illustrative high-coverage envelope, not formal upper bound.

us_model_definition.note: Management/professional/sales/office; original paper used CPS SOC categories and not ISCO major groups.

methodological_gaps: One-digit Eurostat ISCO group OC5 merges sales (SOC 41) with non-cognitive services; cannot resolve C without sub-major groups.
ISCO OC3 mixes technical and associate-professional groups; not all detailed occupations can be assumed to match U.S. SOC 11-29.
One-to-many SOC↔ISCO codes require a reviewed occupational concordance, preferably with 3/4-digit microdata and weights.
These three proportions are illustrative classification sensitivity exercises, not formal statistical intervals or observed shares of occupations exposed to AI.
Unemployed occupational origin and C↔N cross-group flows are not in this employed-person snapshot; no information on model mobility mu.
